question: How does an order get placed and paid?
title: Placing an order
summary: The checkout page asks the API for an order; the API only stores a pending record. A worker loop turns it into one charge at the payment provider, then polls the provider until the bank has answered.

anchor.text:
# The payment provider, as the shop talks to it. Charges are created by the worker (payments/charge.go);
# the provider then sends the customer to their bank for 3-D Secure and calls the webhook below when it knows.
provider:
  name: examplepay
  apiBase: https://api.examplepay.test/v1
  # auto: 3-D Secure only when the bank asks for it; always: every charge.
  threeDSecure: auto
  webhook:
    path: /api/payments/webhook
    events: [charge.succeeded, charge.failed, charge.expired]
  # A charge the bank has not answered in this time expires on the provider's side.
  chargeTimeout: 15m
  retries: 3

steps.lead: First pass on a pending order: `processOrder` calls `BuildCharge` (worker/worker.go:96). The order's lines become charge items that must add up to its total (payments/charge.go:41-54).
steps.details: A coupon becomes one negative line (:48); lines that do not add up fail the order before anything is charged. The customer's address never goes to the provider: only amounts, names and the order's reference.

steps.title: Everything goes into one charge request with the order's key
steps.lead: The amount, the order's reference and the return address go into one `ChargeRequest`, with the idempotency key `charge-<key>` (payments/charge.go:67).
steps.details: Watch the key: it is made from the order's own key, so a create retried after a timeout is the same charge at the provider, never a second one. Orders of 500.00 or more always ask for 3-D Secure (:73-75).

steps.lead: Before this, `Reserve` (worker/worker.go:90) holds the stock; a sold-out line fails the order before anyone is charged.
steps.details: Then the charge is created at the provider (`Payments.Create`). A passing error puts it back to pending and retries later (:102-104); any other error releases the stock and fails it. On success the order becomes `charging`, message "Confirm the payment with your bank", and a deadline is set: the worker's `Timeout` is 20 min (cmd/shop/main.go:32).

steps.lead: No code in this repo talks to the bank. The provider sends the customer to their bank's 3-D Secure page and calls the shop's webhook when it knows the answer.
steps.details: How often that happens is set here: `threeDSecure: auto` (line 7: only when the bank asks for it). Note the charge expires on the provider's side after 15 minutes (line 12). I did not read the provider's code; the events are what `ChargeIssues` expects (payments/status.go:43).

steps.lead: Once the customer confirms (or does not), the bank answers the provider, which marks the charge succeeded, failed or expired and posts a webhook to the shop.
steps.details: The shop has no handle on that exchange: per the comment at payments/status.go:41-42 all it sees is what the provider reports, so it reads the charge's failure text and matches the bank's decline wording with regexes (:36-38). These are called from `processOrder` (worker/worker.go:128).

steps.lead: The checkout learns about the payment by polling `GET /api/orders/{id}` every 3 s (web/src/checkout/waitForPayment.ts:8), showing the server's message when it changes, and returns on paid, failed or cancelled.
steps.details: The order page does the same with a 3 s refetch (web/src/api/orders.ts:6). Watch out: the page gives up after 10 minutes (web/src/checkout/Checkout.vue:17) while the worker allows a charge 20 (step 7). When the page gives up first, the order keeps going on the server; the message says so (:34).
